articles.headline: Altico’s funding warning arrived before the event—but the replay is a diagnostic, not a forecast
articles.dek: Altico’s disclosed commercial-paper reliance appeared well before its default. The chronology supports a funding-risk hypothesis, but the construction-PIT record cannot validate a real-time forecast.
articles.body_markdown:
*This is not current news and is not a forecast. It is a historical replay of Altico, which defaulted on 2019-09-12. Similar mechanisms do not imply the same outcome at another institution or in another market.*

The balance sheet likely to feel stress first is not necessarily the lender with the weakest-looking assets. It may be one that must repeatedly refinance when confidence changes. Altico is a bounded example. Its earliest recorded funding signal was commercial-paper reliance of 29% at 2017-03-31, labelled rollover-freeze exposure. The funding index was 23.7, while the band was stable. That is a filing-period signal about disclosed liability structure—not evidence that a crisis had begun, and not a market-price signal.

The replay assigns a knowledge-time proxy of 2017-05-30, using period end plus 60 days, and records a 27-month lead to default. That sequence is informative but not investable proof. The historical record is PERIOD_END_PROXY_CONSTRUCTION_PIT, lacks a bitemporal input contract, is not eligible as a validated backtest or real-money record, and explicitly says lead times are optimistic.

## The record before the event

Altico’s scoreable funding lens, rather than its PCA field, supplies the earliest recorded warning. The PCA record has no first action zone and no PCA lead-month value. The funding flag says only that commercial-paper reliance created rollover-freeze exposure. Its stable band is an important restraint: a visible vulnerability is not equivalent to an imminent failure call.

The wider summaries establish possibility, not a universal ordering. Of 15 failed institutions in the PCA summary, 5 entered an action zone first, with a median lead of 41 months. Of the same 15, 10 had liability disclosures; the funding signal fired first for 4, with a median lead of 38 months. The India diagnostic covers 48 institutions across two decades and reports 88.9% of non-fraud failures flagged, with a median lead of 21.5 months.

Those results are reconstructions under filing-availability assumptions. They cannot establish that every relevant disclosure was available to a decision-maker at the reconstructed time. The [Failure Radar board](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/board) and [historical validation record](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/validation) retain that eligibility boundary.

## What the lenses saw

The funding lens saw a disclosed liability mix: commercial paper represented 29% at the cited period end. A lender dependent on repeated issuance has a specific vulnerability if refinancing becomes unavailable. It may need replacement cash or other balance-sheet actions under time pressure.

But the dossier does not identify a particular creditor, failed issuance, liquidity reserve, asset-quality trend, management action, or contemporaneous market repricing. It does not establish that every proposed step in a pressure chain occurred at Altico. The correct reading is narrower: disclosed funding dependence preceded a recorded default.

The PCA lens did not offer an earlier action-zone signal here. That does not prove funding measures are superior to supervisory-style tripwires. It shows that the lenses address different failure pathways and can disagree in timing.

Nor should disclosed-data screening be mistaken for forensic detection. The validation note says filings later shown falsified can appear compliant to a threshold engine, with the forensic screen owning those cases. Altico is not fraud-masked in this dossier. That classification does not turn absent evidence into evidence of calm.

## Why the warning mattered

Commercial paper can be efficient in ordinary conditions. Its distinctive risk is not simply cost; it is the need to obtain market consent again and again. A refusal or delay can compress the time available for balance-sheet decisions before assets run off or other funding is secured.

That creates a plausible chain: refinancing reliance can create rollover risk; rollover risk can force defensive liquidity or asset actions; those actions can affect confidence; weaker confidence can make subsequent refinancing harder. This is a model derivation from a disclosed liability structure, not a demonstrated causal narrative of Altico’s final months.

The distinction is essential. A filing-period signal identifies what accounts disclosed. A market-price signal would describe repricing in traded instruments. The dossier supplies the former for Altico, not the latter. A model derivation explains why the disclosed feature might matter; it must not be presented as an observed event.

## The strongest counter-case

The counter-case defeats any simple thesis. A 29% commercial-paper share may be a manageable funding choice rather than a precursor to distress. A lender may roll paper reliably, hold liquidity, use alternative funding, or manage asset and liability timing in ways this observation cannot see. Altico’s stable band supports that caution.

The aggregate evidence is also limited. The hazard panel contains 205 rows, 9 events, and 27 institutions, while 179 censored or unusable rows were excluded. Its leave-one-institution-out AUC was 0.752, with an interval from 0.338 to 1.0. The heuristic AUC was 0.799 on the same held-out rows. The temporal diagnostic AUC was 0.645, below the 0.65 gate, and remains diagnostic only.

The counter-case is therefore central: Altico may be an intelligible historical chronology without being reliable evidence that comparable commercial-paper reliance predicts failure elsewhere. The construction-PIT diagnostic cannot promote into a forecast claim.

## What today's board shares

Today’s board is separate from the Altico replay. As of 2026-10-01, it contains 1 yellow institution and 2 green institutions: Belstar Microfinance Limited, Annapurna Finance Private Limited, and Arohan Financial Services Limited. Their cited filing date is 2026-03-31 and their age is 7 months. Their scores are 77.8, 96.5, and 97.1, respectively; no signals fired are listed.

Yellow is not a credit rating or a prediction of failure. Under the published rule, it may reflect deterioration, a level threshold, a funding flag, a forensic indicator, or a fresh authoritative market drawdown condition. The board excludes 36 stale institutions. Its method does not present quarterly filings older than 183 days or annual filings older than 400 days as current. Institutions without vetted dossiers are absent by design: nothing is scored from memory.

Market data were as of 2026-09-30 and retrieved on 2026-10-01. The market layer is fresh and clock-authoritative, but it has no admission, publication, or tier authority. Admitted canonical records are 0/25, while display rights and expected-record approvals are absent. It cannot upgrade the current tier story. See the [market evidence record](https://api.liquilens.in/api/evidence/markets).

## The next falsifiable test

The thesis weakens if future vetted disclosures show comparable refinancing reliance commonly persisting without liquidity strain, or if stressed institutions more often lack prior disclosed funding vulnerability. It also fails as a useful model if a prospective bitemporal dataset finds no discrimination beyond simpler disclosed-data heuristics.

A credible test needs actual publication times rather than the period-end-plus-60-days proxy, preserved missing disclosures, and outcomes unavailable when a signal was formed. It must not assign model or tier authority to unapproved market data. Until that work exists, historical lead times remain reconstructions rather than promises.

## Follow the pressure chain

The product boundaries are deliberately separate. [LiquiLens](https://liquilens.in/replay/altico/) covers **institution and lender balance-sheet risk**. [Seiche](https://api.seiche.info/api/overview) covers **system dollar-funding capacity**. [Undertow](https://api.seiche.info/undertow/board.json) covers **market liquidity and executable exit capacity**.

These questions can move together without becoming interchangeable. System funding conditions are not an institution filing signal. An institution’s disclosed liability structure is not a traded-market price. Exit capacity is not proof of either balance-sheet solvency or refinancing access. The [LiquiLens research archive](https://liquilens.in/research/) is a research record, not a substitute for those distinctions.

## Sources, method, and limits

This article draws on the [Failure Radar board](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/board), [historical validation](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/validation), [market evidence](https://api.liquilens.in/api/evidence/markets), [Altico replay](https://liquilens.in/replay/altico/), and [replay archive](https://liquilens.in/replay/). Publication date: 2026-10-01.

Altico’s filing observation is 2017-03-31; its availability proxy is 2017-05-30; its default date is 2019-09-12. Current institution filings cited here are as of 2026-03-31, while the market layer is as of 2026-09-30. This is a bounded historical interpretation of disclosed-data diagnostics. Its construction-PIT, missing-data, staleness, fraud-masking, rights, and authority limits are part of the finding, not footnotes to it. Research and market data, not investment advice.

articles.headline: Abhyudaya’s replay: an asset-quality breach arrived before the recorded event
articles.dek: Abhyudaya Co-operative Bank entered an RBI action zone on disclosed NNPA before its recorded default date. The replay is a filing-period signal, not a market-price call or a live forecast—and its proxy clocks materially limit the claim.
articles.body_markdown:
This is a historical replay, not current news and not a forecast. Abhyudaya Co-operative Bank’s recorded default date is 2023-11-24. The narrow proposition is that its first disclosed RBI action-zone breach was an asset-quality signal that appeared before that event. It is not proof that the breach caused the outcome, that the signal was tradable, or that another institution with a similar disclosure will fail.

Three categories must remain separate. A filing-period signal records what a disclosed balance-sheet measure showed for a reporting period. A market-price signal records repricing in traded instruments. A model derivation turns inputs into a score, tier or diagnostic. They may point in the same direction, but they do not share an observation clock, an evidentiary status or a causal meaning. This article concerns the first category: a disclosure-based replay.

LiquiLens covers **institution and lender balance-sheet risk**. It is not a credit rating and this is not investment advice. The supporting record is available at the [Abhyudaya replay](https://liquilens.in/replay/abhyudaya-co-operative-bank/) and the [Failure Radar board](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/board).

## The record before the event

The first recorded action-zone entry was for the period ending 2021-03-31, identified as FY2021. The recorded breach was NNPA. The replay applies a knowledge-time proxy of 2021-05-30: an explicit publication clock when present, otherwise period end plus a 60-day filing-lag proxy. On that convention, the interval to the recorded default date is 29 months.

That is a constructed chronology, not a preserved contemporaneous market record. The historical evidence is labelled PERIOD_END_PROXY_CONSTRUCTION_PIT. It is not validated-backtest eligible, not real-money eligible, and does not have a bitemporal input contract. The dossier explicitly says lead times are optimistic. A period-end measure can be economically relevant before it is publicly available; conversely, a proxy availability date cannot demonstrate when every creditor, depositor or market participant understood its significance.

Abhyudaya is not fraud-masked in this record. Its funding lens was scoreable, but it has no first funding signal. That leaves the NNPA breach as the earliest recorded signal in this replay, not as confirmation that funding conditions were calm or that the asset-quality measure contained the entire explanation.

## What the lenses saw

The PCA/SAF lens saw an NNPA breach. The funding lens did not fire first. That asymmetry is the case’s usable observation: this disclosure framework identified stress first on the asset side.

The broader PCA summary includes 15 failed institutions. Five entered an action zone first, with median lead of 41 months. The funding summary also includes 15 failed institutions, but liability disclosures exist for 10; a funding signal fired first for four, with median lead of 38 months. These are replay descriptions, not failure probabilities, and they do not establish that one lens should always lead another.

The India evidence index covers 48 institutions across two decades and reports 88.9% of non-fraud failures flagged, with median lead of 21.5 months. That headline carries the same construction-PIT qualification. The [validation record](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/validation) reports a temporal AUC of 0.645 against a 0.65 gate. The gate did not pass; construction-PIT diagnostics cannot promote.

A model derivation adds another layer of restraint. The hazard panel contains 205 rows, nine events and 27 institutions, after 179 censored or unusable rows were excluded. Its leave-one-institution-out AUC is 0.752, while the heuristic comparison is 0.799 on the same held-out rows. Those figures describe a limited diagnostic exercise. They do not validate a live ranking, and they do not improve the evidentiary status of Abhyudaya’s filing-period breach.

## Why the warning mattered

An NNPA breach can matter because asset impairment may reduce a lender’s tolerance for further deterioration. It can make earnings, capital, funding confidence and management options more consequential. But the ratio itself is not a mechanism that mechanically causes default. The replay supports a sequence—disclosed asset-quality stress before the recorded event—not a complete causal account.

The published quadrant rule treats any RBI action-zone breach as red. That is a rule-based response to a supervisory threshold, rather than a claim that a fused score is more authoritative than the underlying breach. In Abhyudaya’s case, the rule directs attention to a disclosed constraint on the balance sheet.

The warning therefore mattered as a scrutiny trigger. It said the institution’s asset side had crossed a stated threshold. It did not say when a final event would occur, whether a market instrument should reprice, or whether the liability side would become the immediate source of pressure.

## The strongest counter-case

The strongest counter-case can defeat the thesis: the apparent lead may be largely a hindsight artefact created by proxy dating. Where no explicit publication clock exists, the record uses period end plus 60 days. The dossier calls the resulting lead times optimistic. A later adverse event can make an earlier ratio look more decisive and more actionable than it was in real time.

There is also no independent market-price confirmation available for publication. The market layer is fresh and clocked, but admitted canonical records are 0/25. Rights, display, model-gate and tier-use approvals are absent, and the layer has no admission, publication or tier authority. It must not be used to infer whether securities markets confirmed, anticipated or rejected the filing-period signal.

Nor does the absence of a funding signal resolve that uncertainty. The funding lens sees only institutions with liability disclosures. Missingness is not reassurance. The dossier also warns that institutions whose filings were later shown falsified can appear compliant to a threshold engine; the forensic screen owns those cases.

## What today’s board shares

The current board is not an Abhyudaya forecast analogue. As of 2026-09-30, it shows zero red, one orange, three yellow and 15 green institutions among fresh vetted public dossiers. A further 21 institutions were excluded as stale. Institutions without vetted dossiers are absent by design; nothing is scored from memory.

Utkarsh Small Finance Bank is orange, using a filing as of 2025-03-31, aged 18 months, with score 74.9 and no signals fired. Belstar Microfinance Limited is yellow, using 2026-03-31, aged six months, with score 77.8 and no signals fired. ESAF Small Finance Bank is yellow, using 2025-09-30, aged 12 months, with score 66.0 and no signals fired. These are board entries under published rules, not ratings, predictions or evidence that any named institution resembles Abhyudaya’s path.

The available market layer is as of 2026-09-29 and was retrieved on 2026-09-30. Its lack of publication and tier authority prevents it from decorating those institutional observations with market-price claims.

## The next falsifiable test

The thesis weakens if prospectively preserved filings with actual publication times show that comparable asset-quality action-zone entries do not provide earlier or more informative warning than other lenses. It weakens as well if timely liability disclosures reliably lead such breaches in the relevant population.

The necessary test is prospective rather than reconstructed: retain original filing vintages, record actual availability times, preserve missingness, and compare the first signal with later stress without letting amended history rewrite the information set. Until that record exists, Abhyudaya is a disciplined historical clue, not a validated forecast.

## Follow the pressure chain

Start with the [institution replay](https://liquilens.in/replay/abhyudaya-co-operative-bank/), then compare the [current board](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/board) and [validation file](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/validation). Keep **system dollar-funding capacity** separate through [Seiche’s overview](https://api.seiche.info/api/overview). Keep market liquidity and executable exit capacity separate through the [Undertow board](https://api.seiche.info/undertow/board.json).

That separation prevents a filing-period balance-sheet observation from being mistaken for a system-funding measure or a market-exit measure. A market repricing signal, where authorized and observable, would be a different input. A tier remains a published rule over published components.

## Sources, method, and limits

The relevant materials are the [Failure Radar board](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/board), [historical validation file](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/validation), [market evidence index](https://api.liquilens.in/api/evidence/markets), [Abhyudaya replay](https://liquilens.in/replay/abhyudaya-co-operative-bank/), [Seiche overview](https://api.seiche.info/api/overview), [Undertow board](https://api.seiche.info/undertow/board.json), and the [LiquiLens research archive](https://liquilens.in/research/).

Abhyudaya’s relevant clocks are 2021-03-31 for the filing period, 2021-05-30 for the knowledge-time proxy, and 2023-11-24 for the recorded default date. Those clocks are not interchangeable. Historical results remain construction-PIT rather than validated-backtest or real-money evidence. The market layer remains visible but unauthorized for publication or tier use. Those constraints are not footnotes; they define the claim that can responsibly be made.

articles.headline: United Western Bank’s first disclosed fault line was asset quality, not funding
articles.dek: The replay places an NNPA action-zone breach before United Western Bank’s recorded default, while the scoreable funding lens produced no first signal. That sequence is informative, but its timing is a construction-PIT availability proxy, not a tradable forecast.
articles.body_markdown:
*This is a historical replay, not current news and not a forecast. It examines disclosures associated with United Western Bank before its recorded default on 2006-09-02. Similar mechanisms do not imply the same outcome at another institution.*

United Western Bank offers a narrow answer to the desk question: the earliest disclosed pressure point in this replay was asset quality. The record identifies an NNPA breach in the PCA action zone for the period ended 2001-03-31, assigns a knowledge-time proxy of 2001-05-30, and measures a 63-month lead to default. The funding module was scoreable, yet it produced no first signal.

That is a sequencing observation, not a claim that an NNPA threshold determines failure. A filing-period signal says what a reported balance-sheet measure showed at period end. An availability proxy estimates when that disclosure may have been knowable. A market-price signal would show separate contemporaneous repricing. A model derivation summarizes a rule or statistical relationship built from a dataset. This case supplies the first, proxies the second, does not supply the third, and should not be enlarged into the fourth.

## The record before the event

The public-disclosure replay identifies United Western Bank’s first PCA action-zone entry in FY2001, for the period ending 2001-03-31. The stated breach is NNPA. The case is not marked fraud-masked. The replay assigns its knowledge-time proxy to 2001-05-30 and measures 63 months to the default date of 2006-09-02.

Those facts establish an observed order, not inevitability or a complete causal history. The record does not show every later management decision, creditor response, liability movement, recovery path, or shock. Nor does it establish that outside users possessed the same information at the proxy date. A reporting date is not itself a public-knowledge date.

The funding result is limited rather than reassuring. The module was scoreable, but no first signal is recorded. That means the available liability-disclosure lens did not provide the first recorded alert. It does not certify stable funding, exclude later funding stress, or demonstrate calm. The funding lens only sees institutions that disclose a liability series, so missing liability disclosure remains a material boundary rather than a benign result.

## What the lenses saw

The PCA lens saw the asset-quality action-zone breach first. In the historical validation summary, 15 failed institutions are included; 5 entered an action zone first, with a median lead of 41 months. This is a public-disclosure replay of RBI PCA/SAF tripwires, not a complete account of information available to a lender, depositor, supervisor, or market participant. The underlying framework can be inspected through the [failure-radar board](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/board) and [historical validation record](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/validation).

The funding lens did not fire first here. Across the same summary, 10 of 15 failed institutions have liability disclosures; a funding signal fired first for 4, with a median lead of 38 months. Funding can therefore lead in observable cases. But the result does not show that funding should have led in this case, because observation depends on disclosure and the available series is not a complete map of all funding channels.

A broader India diagnostic covers 48 institutions across two decades and reports that 88.9% of non-fraud failures were flagged, with a median lead of 21.5 months. Its evidence is period-end-proxy construction PIT. It is not validated-backtest eligible, not real-money eligible, and has no bitemporal input contract. The [evidence index](https://api.liquilens.in/api/evidence/markets) is useful for inspection, but a construction diagnostic is not evidence of executable performance.

## Why the warning mattered

The warning mattered because it located disclosed pressure in asset quality before the replay recorded a funding alert. That differs sharply from saying funding was already broken. An asset-quality tripwire can identify a balance-sheet area requiring scrutiny before losses, capital pressure, earnings weakness, funding sensitivity, or confidence effects are fully visible in the available record.

The case supports only a modest proposition: the balance sheet that feels disclosed stress first may be the one whose asset-quality threshold has already been crossed, even if another lens is silent. It does not establish a universal ordering among assets, capital, funding, and market pricing. It also does not turn NNPA into a calibrated probability of default.

A market-price signal remains a separate category of evidence. The current market layer uses Yahoo Finance daily closes, auto-adjusted, and is fresh as of 2026-09-28. But market-derived display, admission, model-gate, and tier use lack approval; admitted canonical records are 0/25. Clock and knowledge fields do not authorize publication or tier use. Those governance limits prevent current market data from being retrofitted into this historical case.

## The strongest counter-case

The counter-case can defeat the thesis. This may be retrospective pattern recognition: because United Western Bank later defaulted, an earlier breach can appear more decisive after the fact than it was when disclosed. The replay uses an explicit publication clock when present; otherwise it uses period end plus 60 days. Its evidence states that lead times are optimistic. Actual availability could differ from the assigned proxy.

The threshold may also not have been the most informative signal in a fully reconstructed record. Funding could have deteriorated through channels not captured by the disclosed liability series. Other facts may have been known to creditors or supervisors. The absence of a first funding signal is therefore missing explanatory power, not affirmative evidence of resilience.

The model record adds restraint. The temporal diagnostic reports an AUC of 0.645 against a 0.65 gate and does not pass. The hazard result reports AUC of 0.752, while the comparison heuristic reports 0.799 on the same held-out rows. These are model derivations and diagnostics, not grounds to promote the replay into a validated prediction engine.

Threshold systems also cannot uncover concealed facts. The PCA note says filings later shown falsified can look compliant to a threshold engine; the forensic screen owns those cases. United Western Bank is not fraud-masked, but that limitation still constrains the inference.

Today’s board is a separate screen, not an extension of the United Western replay. As of 2026-09-29 it has 0 red, 1 orange, 3 yellow, and 15 green institutions; 21 are excluded as stale. Institutions without vetted dossiers are absent by design rather than scored from memory. Current board context is available from the [failure-radar board](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/board).

articles.headline: Sambandh Finserve’s funding signal arrived early—but could not see through fraud
articles.dek: The historical replay identifies wholesale leverage as Sambandh Finserve’s first disclosed funding warning. It is a liability-side clue, not a market verdict, a causal proof, or a validated prediction of default.
articles.body_markdown:
*This is not current news and is not a forecast. It is a historical replay of Sambandh Finserve, which defaulted on 2020-10-13. Similar mechanisms do not imply the same outcome elsewhere.*

The balance sheet that should have felt pressure first was Sambandh Finserve’s funding structure. The evidence does not show that a model foresaw default, or that a market price confirmed an approaching event. It shows something narrower: on 2016-03-31, disclosed wholesale leverage was 8.51x, above the funding lens’s 7x flag, and the lens classified the institution as fragile.

Under the replay’s availability convention, that filing-period observation became knowable on 2016-05-30, using period end plus a 60-day proxy where an explicit publication clock is unavailable. That is 52 months before the default date. It is an early filing-derived signal. It is not evidence that creditors repriced Sambandh on that date, nor proof that the disclosed leverage caused the eventual failure.

The crucial complication is that Sambandh is fraud-masked. Where filings were later shown to be falsified, threshold engines can make an institution look compliant. A leverage flag can identify vulnerability in what was disclosed; it cannot recover risks concealed from disclosure. The forensic screen owns that blind spot.

## The record before the event

Three clocks must remain separate. The reporting period ended on 2016-03-31. The construction-PIT proxy places public availability on 2016-05-30. The institution defaulted on 2020-10-13. Treating the first date as immediate public knowledge would overstate what an outside creditor, investor, or analyst could have known.

The funding record supplies one stated first flag: wholesale leverage 8.51x >= 7x. The band is fragile. The PCA record has no first action-zone entry and no recorded lead months. That absence is not a clean bill of health. It means only that this replay does not identify a PCA action-zone signal before the event.

The historical evidence is explicitly `PERIOD_END_PROXY_CONSTRUCTION_PIT`. It is not validated-backtest eligible, not real-money eligible, and does not have a bitemporal input contract. Its availability basis is an explicit publication clock when present, otherwise period end plus 60 days. Lead times are therefore optimistic. This is a disciplined reconstruction of a possible information set, not a verified record of every participant’s information set.

The [Sambandh replay](https://liquilens.in/replay/sambandh-finserve/) is consequently more useful as a question for due diligence than as a retrospective claim of foresight.

## What the lenses saw

The funding lens saw a liability-side exposure: reliance implied by elevated wholesale leverage. The economic proposition is conditional. A lender with greater refinancing dependence can be more sensitive to creditor confidence and rollover conditions. If refinancing capacity contracts, liquidity preservation or balance-sheet adjustment can become more urgent. The dossier does not establish the specific creditor actions, liquidity movements, or operational sequence between the flag and default.

The PCA lens did not provide a recorded action-zone lead. The funding signal therefore stands alone as the first visible balance-sheet warning in this case. It should not be inflated into confirmation from a second lens.

Nor does the broader model stack repair that gap. The conformal alarm remains a diagnostic, while its historical tier wiring is suspended pending prospective revalidation; it has no score or tier authority. The hazard temporal test recorded AUC of 0.645 against a 0.65 gate and did not pass. Construction-PIT diagnostics cannot promote.

Those are model-derivation facts, not market facts. They describe how the analytical apparatus performed on its limited record. They do not report a traded price, a creditor withdrawal, or an independently observed funding squeeze.

## Why the warning mattered

The warning mattered because funding fragility can be visible before a public case for failure is established. Reported asset stress may emerge slowly, while a wholesale-funded institution can remain exposed to a change in creditors’ willingness to extend or renew financing.

Yet “mattered” must not become “predicted.” Wholesale leverage above a threshold identifies a reason to investigate the funding stack, its maturity profile, creditor concentration, refinancing options, and the quality of the underlying disclosures. It does not establish an imminent event. The 52-month interval is especially important: the record supports an early vulnerability signal, not a timing tool.

The wider funding summary reinforces that restraint. Among 15 failed institutions, 10 had liability disclosures usable by the funding lens. The funding signal fired first in 4 cases, with median lead of 38 months. Those are descriptive results from disclosed series, not a calibrated probability of default. The [historical validation record](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/validation) preserves those eligibility limits.

## The strongest counter-case

The strongest counter-case can defeat the thesis. Wholesale leverage may be too broad and too slow-moving to support a decision beyond additional investigation. It fired first in only 4 cases in the disclosed-liability record, and Sambandh’s fraud-masked status makes the reported balance sheet an unusually weak basis for a complete diagnosis. If the core condition was concealed, the signal may have described only a peripheral vulnerability.

The long gap to default further weakens any claim of near-term usefulness. A flag that precedes an event by 52 months may distinguish fragility from resilience, but it may also impose years of false urgency. The period-end proxy can also manufacture apparent lead: a fully bitemporal record could materially change when information was actually available.

A sceptical reader can therefore conclude that the replay offers no verified causal chain, no validated trading or credit signal, and no proof that public disclosures revealed the institution’s true condition. articles.headline: New India Co-operative Bank showed a disclosed stress breach before the event — and the fraud boundary is the point
articles.dek: A historical replay finds an NNPA action-zone breach at the FY2021 period end, ahead of the later default date. It supports investigation of disclosed balance-sheet pressure, not confidence that a threshold screen can see through false accounts.
articles.body_markdown:
*This is a historical replay, not current news and not a forecast. It examines the public record before New India Co-operative Bank’s default date of 2025-02-13. Similar mechanisms do not imply the same outcome elsewhere.*

The desk question has a conditional answer. On the disclosed record, New India Co-operative Bank should have drawn attention through an asset-quality signal: an NNPA breach placing it in the RBI PCA/SAF action zone for the period ended 2021-03-31, labelled FY2021. The replay uses 2021-05-30 as its knowledge-time proxy and records a 44-month lead to default.

That is a filing-period signal. It is not proof that the published balance sheet described the institution’s actual condition, and it is not a market-price signal or a model result. The dossier marks this case fraud-masked. That qualification is decisive: a reported threshold crossing warrants investigation, but cannot deliver a forensic account of a bank whose filings may have been unreliable.

## The record before the event

Three clocks must remain separate. The filing period ended on 2021-03-31. Where no explicit publication clock is available, the replay uses period end plus 60 days, producing the 2021-05-30 knowledge-time proxy. The default occurred on 2025-02-13. None is a current-market timestamp, or evidence of what management, supervisors, depositors, or counterparties knew privately.

The PCA/SAF lens replays public disclosure against the RBI’s action-zone tripwires. It can identify a reported threshold breach, not establish causation, reconstruct undisclosed cash movements, assess intent, or verify that the reported inputs were true. The [New India replay](https://liquilens.in/replay/new-india-co-operative-bank/) is evidence of what a disclosure screen could flag from the available record.

Fraud-masked is not a footnote. Institutions whose filings were later shown falsified can appear compliant to a threshold engine. Even this early visible breach cannot establish whether reported deterioration captured the full problem, its first stage, or only part of it. A disclosure warning can be useful and materially incomplete at once.

## What the lenses saw

The PCA/SAF lens saw the NNPA breach. The funding lens produced no first signal for New India. That is missing evidence, not evidence of stable funding: the funding lens only sees institutions that disclose a liability series. No funding signal cannot become a funding all-clear.

Across 15 failed institutions, 5 entered the PCA/SAF action zone first, with a median lead of 41 months. The funding summary has liability disclosures for 10 of those 15 institutions; its signal fired first for 4, with a median lead of 38 months. These are replay descriptions, not prospective accuracy claims.

The wider India diagnostic covers 48 institutions across two decades and says 88.9% of non-fraud failures were flagged, with a median lead of 21.5 months. Yet it is explicitly PERIOD_END_PROXY_CONSTRUCTION_PIT: not eligible as a validated backtest or real-money test, without a bitemporal input contract, and with optimistic lead times. The [validation record](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/validation) and [market evidence index](https://api.liquilens.in/api/evidence/markets) retain those limits.

A model derivation is separate again. The hazard panel contains 205 rows, 9 events, and 27 institutions. Its leave-one-institution-out AUC is 0.752, while the heuristic reaches 0.799 on the same held-out rows. Its temporal diagnostic AUC is 0.645, below the 0.65 gate, and remains diagnostic only. Those results describe a constrained construction exercise; they do not show that New India was predictably destined to fail.

## Why the warning mattered

A disclosed action-zone breach changes the question from whether an institution looks routine to whether reported asset quality, loss absorption, disclosure quality, and possible funding vulnerability warrant deeper scrutiny.

If reported condition is genuine, pressure may move from asset quality into loss absorption, confidence, funding, and resilience to further losses. But that is a pressure chain, not a demonstrated causal sequence here. New India has an asset-side warning and no funding first signal. Its fraud-masked designation means disclosures may not have measured the actual condition fully. Investigation, rather than a tidy narrative of linear deterioration, is the warranted inference.

The 44-month lead is both meaningful and hazardous. It identifies an early public point at which the disclosed record crossed a regulatory threshold. But a long replay lead can make a threshold engine appear to have seen more than historical filings could reveal.

## The strongest counter-case

The counter-case can defeat any broad thesis. New India does not establish that disclosed thresholds reliably forecast institutional failure. An NNPA breach is not proof of insolvency, liquidity failure, misconduct, or an impending default. Fraud-masked cases sharpen the objection: a system built from public disclosures cannot claim forensic sight when the disclosures themselves may be unreliable.

Timing is another objection. The replay uses explicit publication time when present and otherwise a period-end-plus-60-days proxy. That can make lead times optimistic. Without a bitemporal input contract, the record cannot prove what a live user could access on each historical date. The conformal alarm is diagnostic, with no score or tier authority pending prospective revalidation.

A later event also does not retroactively prove decision usefulness. The heuristic’s stronger held-out AUC and the failed temporal gate limit the model conclusion. The defensible thesis is narrower: disclosed action-zone pressure is a reason to investigate earlier, while fraud and missing disclosures limit what the investigation can infer.

## What today's board shares

Today’s board is separate from this replay. As of 2026-09-27, the Failure Radar shows 0 red institutions, 1 orange, 3 yellow, and 15 green. Utkarsh Small Finance Bank is orange, based on a 2025-03-31 filing aged 18 months, with a score of 74.9. Belstar Microfinance Limited is yellow, based on 2026-03-31 and aged 6 months, with a score of 77.8. ESAF Small Finance Bank is yellow, based on 2025-09-30 and aged 12 months, with a score of 66.0.

These are published-rule screen outputs, not credit ratings or forecasts. The board excludes 21 stale institutions. Institutions without vetted dossiers are absent by design; absence is not a clean bill of health. The [Failure Radar board](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/board) is not a current extension of the New India case.

The market layer was available as of 2026-09-25 and retrieved on 2026-09-27, but has no admission, publication, or tier authority. Approval checks were incomplete for every expected canonical record. Thus a market-price signal cannot upgrade or downgrade institutional tiers. Fresh prices are not authority to publish a risk classification.

## The next falsifiable test

The thesis weakens if institutions crossing disclosed action-zone thresholds do not later show persistent, independently disclosed balance-sheet pressure more often than comparable institutions that do not cross them. It also weakens if prospective testing with actual publication timestamps, rather than period-end proxies, fails to retain useful separation.

A persuasive test must distinguish a filing-period signal from a market-price signal and from a model derivation. It must establish what was public, when it was public, whether it was accurate, and whether it added information beyond simpler disclosure rules. A later event alone cannot satisfy those tests.

Those boundaries matter. Seiche’s composite is 41.5 and labelled EROSION, with guarded confidence; its note says slow-moving or modelled structure leads current market confirmation. Undertow contains partial segments. Neither a system-plumbing reading nor an executable-exit reading proves New India’s historical balance-sheet condition, fills an unavailable liability disclosure, or overcomes a fraud-masked filing record.

## Sources, method, and limits

This article uses only the supplied evidence dossier and permitted sources, including the [New India replay](https://liquilens.in/replay/new-india-co-operative-bank/), [historical validation](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/validation), [market evidence](https://api.liquilens.in/api/evidence/markets), [LiquiLens research](https://liquilens.in/research/), and the [Failure Radar board](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/board).

It was not market-price confirmation, not a validated prospective model result, and not a substitute for forensic verification of the accounts.

Research and market data, not investment advice.

articles.body_markdown:

Nedungadi Bank should have appeared under pressure first through disclosed capital, not through a scored funding signal. The narrow thesis is that its CRAR entry into the first RBI action zone in FY1999 was the earliest observable warning in this replay. It preceded the bank’s 2002-11-02 default by 41 months. That does not prove capital caused the default, establish what market participants knew, or show that an investor could have traded a known outcome.

The distinction is central. The CRAR breach is a filing-period signal, subject to an availability proxy. A market-price signal would require authorised market evidence, and none establishes Nedungadi’s historical pathway. A model derivation is a rule or diagnostic built over observed records; it is not itself an observed event. Conflating these categories would turn a limited replay into a claim it cannot support.

This historical replay is **not investment advice** and **not a credit rating**.

## The record before the event

The [Nedungadi Bank replay](https://liquilens.in/replay/nedungadi-bank/) records its first PCA/SAF action-zone entry at the 1999-03-31 period end, labelled FY1999. The breach was CRAR and its status was `threshold_1`. The knowledge-time proxy is 1999-05-30, using the stated 60-day filing lag. It has no bitemporal input contract, is not eligible as a validated backtest, and is not eligible for real-money use. When an explicit publication clock is unavailable, the convention is period end plus 60 days. The dossier explicitly warns that lead times may be optimistic.

Thus, 1999-03-31 is an accounting reference date, while 1999-05-30 is an imposed availability convention. Neither proves every participant received the information simultaneously. The [Failure Radar board](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/board) preserves that separation rather than silently treating period-end information as immediately known.

Nedungadi is marked as not fraud-masked. That means this replay does not assign it to the group in which filings later shown to be falsified can make an institution appear compliant to a threshold engine. It does not establish that disclosed information was complete.

## What the lenses saw

The PCA lens saw the CRAR breach. The funding lens was not scoreable and produced no first signal. This is a missing-data outcome, not a conclusion that funding was calm, stable, or irrelevant. The funding framework can observe only institutions disclosing a liability series; Nedungadi’s record does not support that lens.

The broader summaries remain bounded. Of 15 failed institutions in the PCA summary, 5 entered an action zone first, with a median lead of 41 months. In the funding summary, 10 of 15 failed institutions had liability disclosures, 4 had the funding signal fire first, and the median lead was 38 months. The hazard work cannot repair this gap. Its leave-one-institution-out row AUC is 0.752, and its temporal AUC is 0.645, below the 0.65 diagnostic gate. It cannot complete a causal transmission story. The rule-based `threshold_1` classification is also not a market price. The 41-month lead is a model derivation from a proxy knowledge date and a recorded default date. Neither converts an action-zone breach into a calibrated failure frequency.

## The strongest counter-case

A stronger version of this thesis can fail. One action-zone breach in a construction-PIT record may identify regulatory vulnerability while revealing little about timing, severity, or the eventual failure mechanism. A 41-month lead itself argues against interpreting the result as an imminent-event alarm.

The availability convention may flatter apparent warning time. The record lacks a bitemporal input contract and substitutes period end plus 60 days where no explicit publication clock exists. Even that proxy leaves lead times labelled optimistic. Missing funding evidence is equally ambiguous: absent liability disclosure is not absent funding pressure.

If fully timestamped, contemporaneous liability information had generated an earlier warning, the claim that capital should feel stress first would fail. If a market-price measure had repriced before the filing became knowable, it would answer a different question and also defeat any claim that the filing was the first observable warning overall. The defensible conclusion is narrower: capital was the earliest recorded signal in this replay.

## What today's board shares

Today’s board is not a live continuation of Nedungadi. As of 2026-09-26, it contains 0 red, 1 orange, 3 yellow, and 15 green institutions, while excluding 21 stale institutions. Utkarsh Small Finance Bank is orange on a 2025-03-31 dossier. Belstar Microfinance Limited and ESAF Small Finance Bank are yellow.

These are published-rule screens over vetted public dossiers, not ratings. Yet the current market layer has 0 of 25 admitted canonical records and has no tier or publication authority. It is fresh and clocked, but display and tier use are not approved. The [market evidence endpoint](https://api.liquilens.in/api/evidence/markets) records that boundary.

The thesis weakens if a prospective, fully timestamped filing record shows that action-zone entry does not precede meaningful balance-sheet stress more reliably than available alternatives when disclosure timing is held constant. It also weakens if institutions with disclosed liability series repeatedly generate earlier usable funding warnings and CRAR adds no incremental diagnostic value.

That test must use actual publication timestamps rather than period-end proxies, preserve missing disclosures as missing, and separate forensic cases in which filings can mask weakness. Until then, this remains a historically grounded mechanism claim, not a calibrated forecast.

## Follow the pressure chain

The pressure chain supported here stops at disclosed CRAR weakness, RBI action-zone entry, and eventual default. The funding link is unobserved, not absent. No market-price link is established.

The product boundaries matter: Seiche covers **system dollar-funding capacity**; LiquiLens covers **institution and lender balance-sheet risk**; Undertow covers market liquidity and executable exit capacity. Seiche’s composite is 41.2 and labelled EROSION, with guarded confidence because slow-moving or modelled structure has not been broadly confirmed by current market plumbing. Undertow reports partial coverage across segments. Neither is evidence about Nedungadi’s historical route. See the [Seiche overview](https://api.seiche.info/api/overview) and [Undertow board](https://api.seiche.info/undertow/board.json).

Primary material is the [Nedungadi replay](https://liquilens.in/replay/nedungadi-bank/), the [Failure Radar board](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/board), and the [historical validation endpoint](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/validation). The decisive limits are construction-PIT historical status, no real-money eligibility, no bitemporal input contract, proxy timing that can leave lead times optimistic, no authorised market-derived tier evidence, and unscoreable funding evidence for Nedungadi. Missing evidence is not calm. It is a boundary on what this replay can claim.

articles.headline: First Leasing replay: when a public balance-sheet radar cannot see through the record
articles.dek: First Leasing Company Of India’s fraud-masked default is not an early-warning success. It is a boundary case showing why a filing-period signal, a market-price signal and a model derivation must not be treated as the same evidence.
articles.body_markdown:
*Historical replay — not current news and not a forecast.* First Leasing Company Of India defaulted on 2013-12-02. The useful lesson is not that a public screen called the event. The supplied record does not establish that it did. Rather, it shows a harder limitation: an institution can be under severe economic pressure while its reported balance sheet fails to transmit that pressure to a threshold-based public-data system.

The distinction matters for the desk question: which balance sheet should feel stress first, and why? A filing-period signal describes what disclosed reports showed at an available reporting point. A market-price signal describes repricing in tradable instruments, when the market data are authorized for that use. A model derivation combines permitted inputs under a stated rule. None can be silently substituted for another; none proves the underlying economic condition by itself.

First Leasing is marked `fraud_masked` in this replay. Its case therefore tests the boundary of disclosed-data surveillance, rather than supplying evidence that an ordinary balance-sheet deterioration was identified in time.

## The record before the event

First Leasing Company Of India is classified as an NBFC, with default date 2013-12-02. Its PCA record contains no first action-zone date and no lead-month figure. Its funding record is scoreable, but contains no first signal and no lead-month figure. These are missing replay results, not affirmative findings that funding was calm, capital was adequate or the institution was safe.

The historical framework explicitly warns that institutions whose filings were later shown falsified can look compliant to a threshold engine; the forensic screen owns those cases. That warning is central here. The dossier does not provide underlying accounting particulars that would establish the route from misstatement to default. It does establish that the reported public record did not produce an earlier PCA action-zone entry or funding signal in this replay.

The India evidence is broader but tightly qualified. It covers 48 institutions across two decades, with a headline finding that 88.9% of non-fraud failures were flagged and median lead was 21.5 months. Yet its status is `PERIOD_END_PROXY_CONSTRUCTION_PIT`: it is not validated-backtest eligible, not real-money eligible and has no bitemporal input contract. Availability uses an explicit publication clock when present; otherwise it uses period end plus 60 days. The dossier says lead times are optimistic. These are diagnostic construction results, not tradable performance evidence. See the [Failure Radar board](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/board), [validation record](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/validation) and [First Leasing replay](https://liquilens.in/replay/first-leasing-company-of-india/).

## What the lenses saw

The PCA lens is a public-disclosure replay of the RBI’s PCA/SAF tripwires. Among 15 failed institutions, 5 entered an action zone first, with median lead of 41 months. That is evidence that disclosed supervisory-style thresholds can be informative in some cases. It is not evidence that they identified First Leasing: its supplied PCA fields show no action-zone date and no lead time.

The funding lens is narrower because it requires a disclosed liability series. Of 15 failed institutions, 10 had liability disclosures; the funding signal fired first for 4, with median lead of 38 months. First Leasing is marked scoreable, yet no first funding signal is recorded. That is a non-result in the replay, not a clean bill of health.

A filing-period signal must also be separated from a model derivation. The published rule can fuse disclosed levels, deterioration, a funding flag, a forensic indicator and an authoritative market drawdown into a presentation tier. PD levels are corpus-fitted and prior-corrected to a ~0.25%/yr population base rate using King-Zeng. That makes them model outputs, not direct observations. The conformal alarm is retained only as a diagnostic: its historical tier wiring is suspended and it has no score or tier authority pending prospective revalidation.

A market-price signal is different again. The dossier describes Merton PD as a market repricing signal, not a calibrated failure frequency. For the current market layer, data are fresh and clocked, but display, model-gate and tier use are not approved; admitted canonical records are 0/25. Market information therefore cannot authorize a current tier in this record.

## Why the warning mattered

A reported balance sheet is supposed to connect asset quality, loss absorption and creditor confidence. If losses, impairment or other relevant conditions are not truthfully represented, reported capital and risk measures can remain clear of a threshold. If disclosure does not reveal why liability providers should reassess the institution, a funding lens may not fire either.

That is an inference about the limits of observable inputs, not a reconstructed account of First Leasing’s finances. The dossier supports the narrower conclusion: in a fraud-masked case, apparent compliance in disclosed data may be an artefact of the record rather than evidence of resilience. A missed signal in an honest, timely disclosure regime could challenge the threshold. A missed signal where filings were later shown falsified can instead show that the measured balance sheet was not a reliable map of the institution.

The strongest counter-case can defeat any inflated version of this thesis. Perhaps the framework is simply too weak to identify stress reliably. First Leasing has no recorded PCA or funding lead. Historical availability is sometimes proxied using period end plus 60 days, and the dossier expressly calls the lead times optimistic.

The hazard evidence is also limited. The panel has 205 rows, 9 events and 27 institutions; 179 censored or unusable rows were excluded. Leave-one-institution-out AUC is 0.752, with an interval of 0.338 to 1.0. On the same held-out rows, the heuristic AUC is 0.799, above the hazard AUC. The temporal test has AUC of 0.645, below the 0.65 diagnostic gate, and cannot promote construction-PIT diagnostics.

That critique means this replay cannot demonstrate that the radar would have protected a creditor, investor or supervisor. Nor can a `fraud_masked` label solve forensic identification after the fact. The defensible claim is smaller: the system reports the absence and limits of disclosed signals rather than converting unavailable or compromised evidence into reassurance.

## What today's board shares

The board as of 2026-09-25 has 0 red institutions, 1 orange, 3 yellow and 15 green; 21 stale institutions are excluded. Utkarsh Small Finance Bank is orange, based on a 2025-03-31 filing as-of date aged 18 months, with score 74.9. Belstar Microfinance Limited is yellow as of 2026-03-31, aged 6 months, score 77.8. Nothing older than 24 months is presented as current, while institutions without vetted dossiers are absent by design. ## The next falsifiable test

The thesis weakens if a genuinely bitemporal, prospectively audited sample finds that disclosed PCA, funding and forensic signals do not identify pressure before adverse outcomes better than chance. It gains credibility only if prospective records preserve what was knowable when, retain missing and stale observations instead of filling them with calm, and separately test filing signals, market-price signals and model derivations. This is not investment advice and not a credit rating.

## Follow the pressure chain

The disciplined sequence is reported assets and capital; disclosed liability structure; supervisory-style thresholds; forensic indicators; then market and exit conditions where authority permits. A break should prompt investigation, not automatic certainty.

LiquiLens covers **institution and lender balance-sheet risk**. [Seiche](https://api.seiche.info/api/overview) covers **system dollar-funding capacity**. The question is not whether Altico’s funding flag predicted its default. The dossier cannot support that claim. It can support a narrower observation: Altico’s first funding signal identified commercial-paper reliance of 29% and explicitly described rollover-freeze exposure, even though the funding index sat in a stable band. That contrast makes Altico a useful replay of a balance-sheet question: which institution should be investigated first when reported broad measures look calm but liabilities require recurring refinancing?

This is a screen for inquiry, not a conclusion about creditworthiness. It is **not a credit rating**, not investment advice, and not a prediction of institutional failure.

## The record before the event

Altico defaulted on 2019-09-12. Its recorded first funding signal belongs to the period ending 2017-03-31, with 2017-05-30 used as the knowledge-time proxy. The recorded lead was 27 months. The funding index was 23.7, its band was stable, and the disclosed flag was CP reliance of 29% with rollover-freeze exposure.

Those items are different kinds of evidence. The period-end balance-sheet observation is a filing-period signal. The knowledge-time proxy is an attempted estimate of when that signal could have been available, not proof of an exact public-information clock. The stable band is an output of a funding index. The rollover flag is a component-level warning. None is a market-price signal, and none is a calibrated probability that Altico would fail.

The [Altico replay](https://liquilens.in/replay/altico/) and [Failure Radar board](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/board) preserve this distinction. A stable aggregate band did not erase the disclosed funding feature; it meant that the broad index did not register a more severe state. The replay therefore argues against reading a single band as a clean bill of health.

Liability disclosures were available for 10, the funding signal fired first for 4, and the median lead was 38 months. The India diagnostic describes 48 institutions across two decades and reports 88.9% of non-fraud failures flagged, with a median lead of 21.5 months. It does show a disclosed feature, a later default date, and a recorded lead under a proxy availability convention.

The more defensible lesson is about aggregation. A composite can summarize multiple inputs while a discrete component identifies a vulnerability the composite does not elevate. The dossier calls the resulting lead times optimistic. Without a bitemporal input contract, historical availability and amended values remain material limitations.

More fundamentally, one NNPA breach is not a complete failure narrative. The funding lens did not fire first. The bank is fraud-masked. articles.body_markdown:
## The finding

Utkarsh Small Finance Bank is the balance sheet in this monitored set most likely to register visible financial pressure first. That is a conditional filing-based finding, not a claim that failure is imminent. The current orange tier rests on disclosed asset quality and a modelled monitoring probability, while the evidence needed to establish a funding event or a market repricing is unavailable or inadmissible.

The key disclosed burden is GNPA of 9.4%. The subject dossier is as of 2025-03-31 and is aged 18 months at publication. Its monitored PD_12m is 0.0031, compared with 0.0016 at the FY2024 reference point; delta_pd_12m is 0.0015. Those are model derivations from the filing record, not observed market prices and not a credit rating. The model basis explicitly identifies GNPA 9.4%.

That distinction is central. A filing-period signal says what the reported balance sheet showed at a stated reporting date. A market-price signal would say how tradable claims were priced at an admissible observation time. A model derivation transforms disclosed inputs into a monitoring estimate under stated assumptions. None of those is interchangeable. The orange tier is a prioritisation device for investigation, not an investment recommendation or an assertion of default.

## The mechanism

The proposed mechanism begins with impaired assets. A high GNPA ratio can become an earnings and capital problem if provisioning, recoveries, and operating earnings do not offset the credit burden. Capital then has less capacity to support lending, absorb later shocks, or reassure funding providers. The pressure chain is plausible, but the dossier does not supply a future loss path, recovery path, or provisioning trajectory. It therefore supports a vulnerability thesis, not a completed causal diagnosis.

## What the filings say

The filing-based screen assigns a score of 74.9 and grade A, alongside the adverse GNPA observation. These labels can coexist because they answer different questions. The score is within a corpus-monitoring probability framework and is explicitly not a credit rating. A relatively low modelled probability does not negate a material asset-quality burden; equally, GNPA alone does not establish near-term incapacity.

The historical record carries a major limitation. It is PERIOD_END_PROXY_CONSTRUCTION_PIT, with no complete bitemporal public-availability and revision archive. On that view, the orange designation may be an appropriately cautious reaction to a historical asset-quality burden, rather than evidence that the bank is now approaching balance-sheet incapacity.

The conformal diagnostic also did not alarm: distress was 25.1 against a threshold_distress of 26.799999999999997. But that result cannot exonerate the bank. Its wiring status is SUSPENDED_REVALIDATION_REQUIRED, its gate is CLOSED_REVALIDATION_REQUIRED, and it has no score or tier authority. A suspended diagnostic cannot be used to intensify the thesis or dismiss it.

The counter-case would become materially stronger with a newer vetted filing showing improving GNPA and preserved or increased capital headroom. Admissible liability evidence showing stable funding would strengthen it further. Neither is supplied here.

## The evidence that is dark

The deposit-run lens is dark because there are no consecutive deposit disclosures. Wholesale reliance, CD strain, and LCR headroom are also dark. Those gaps block a full assessment of funding pressure. They do not demonstrate an absence of funding risk.

Forensics are ineligible. There is no forensic verdict and no forensic indicator. That is a missing-data disclosure, not evidence of clean accounts. The dossier itself notes that filings later shown to be falsified can appear compliant to a threshold engine; the forensic screen owns that problem when it is eligible.

The radar excludes 21 stale institutions rather than presenting them as current. Its current comparison rows include Belstar Microfinance Limited, ESAF Small Finance Bank, and IndusInd Bank Ltd in yellow; Utkarsh is the single orange name, with no red names. This is selective monitored coverage of institutions with fresh vetted public dossiers, not a universal ranking of lenders.

## What would change the call

A newer vetted filing could weaken or overturn this view if it showed sustained improvement in GNPA while CRAR remained resilient. The pressure chain would be broken if impaired assets improved, credit costs ceased absorbing capital capacity, and reliable liability disclosures showed no associated funding deterioration.

The thesis would strengthen if GNPA deteriorated, CRAR moved toward the licensing floor, or newly eligible evidence revealed deposit, wholesale, CD, or LCR strain. Future market evidence should enter only after rights, identity, timing, model, and tier-use gates are satisfied. A price observation without those authorities is not a substitute for evidence.

## Follow the pressure chain

Follow the chain from GNPA to provisioning and earnings, from earnings to capital absorption, and from capital capacity to lending flexibility and creditor confidence. Funding is the next link, but it is unlit rather than benign. The relevant research boundary is **institution and lender balance-sheet risk**: that is LiquiLens’s remit.

System conditions belong elsewhere. Seiche addresses **system dollar-funding capacity**, while Undertow addresses **market liquidity and executable exit capacity**. The [Seiche overview](https://api.seiche.info/api/overview) reports an EROSION regime with guarded confidence, led by modelled or slow-moving structure rather than broad current market-plumbing confirmation. The [Undertow board](https://api.seiche.info/undertow/board.json) reports partial coverage across several segments. Neither product supplies an authorised Utkarsh market-price verdict.

## Sources, method, and limits

This article relies only on the supplied [Failure Radar board](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/board), [validation record](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/validation), and [market-evidence index](https://api.liquilens.in/api/evidence/markets). Readers can inspect related [LiquiLens research](https://liquilens.in/research/), [replay material](https://liquilens.in/replay/), and [investigations](https://liquilens.in/investigations/). The [US NDFI watch](https://api.liquilens.in/api/us-radar/ndfi) is separate context and is not evidence about Utkarsh.

Historical validation is diagnostic only. The hazard panel has 205 rows, 9 events, and 27 institutions; its temporal AUC is 0.645, below the 0.65 diagnostic gate. The India replay covers 48 institutions and reports a 21.5-month median lead, but it is filing-availability-proxied construction-PIT and its lead times are explicitly optimistic. Similar historical mechanisms do not establish the same outcome here. This is a current filing-based analysis, not investment advice, and the orange tier is not a credit rating.

articles.headline: Rupee Co-operative Bank replay: the signal was an evidence boundary, not a clean warning
articles.dek: This is a historical replay, not current news and not a forecast. Rupee Co-operative Bank’s record shows why a balance-sheet screen must separate a filing-period signal, a market-price signal, and an absence of scoreable evidence.
articles.body_markdown:
*This is a historical replay, not current news and not a forecast. Similar balance-sheet mechanisms do not imply the same outcome.* Rupee Co-operative Bank defaulted on 2022-09-22. The supplied record does not identify a balance sheet that should have felt stress first through a usable public signal. Its central lesson is narrower, but important: an unscoreable record is an evidence boundary, not a benign result.

That conclusion is not a retrospective claim that the institution was healthy before the event. It is also not a claim that a model detected what the available inputs did not show. A filing-period signal depends on published, scoreable institutional disclosures. A market-price signal depends on an observable market repricing measure. A model derivation is an output constructed from its inputs and assumptions. These are different evidentiary objects, and none can be substituted for another when the record is missing.

A Failure Radar tier is a published rule over published components, not a solvency verdict, a failure prediction, or **not a credit rating**. Rupee Co-operative Bank is a useful hard case precisely because a failed institution need not leave a neat, timely trail for every public screen.

## The record before the event

The replay records Rupee Co-operative Bank as an urban co-operative bank, with the event date of 2022-09-22. Fraud masking is marked false. That means this case is not tagged as one in which later-discovered falsification made apparently compliant filings misleading. It does not establish capital strength, asset quality, liquidity, funding resilience, or prior safety.

The institution-specific PCA record contains no first action-zone observation and no lead time. The funding record is explicitly unscoreable, with no first signal and no lead time. The dossier supplies no historical filing as-of date for the institution. That date cannot be inferred from the default date, the publication date, or a later board timestamp.

The relevant record is therefore the [Rupee Co-operative Bank replay](https://liquilens.in/replay/rupee-co-operative-bank/), not a current institutional dossier. The Failure Radar board is dated 2026-09-01 and its market layer is dated 2026-08-11. Those dates describe later analytical material, not information demonstrably available before Rupee Co-operative Bank’s event.

## What the lenses saw

Read literally, neither named balance-sheet lens supplies a usable lead in this case. The PCA lens does not show a first action-zone breach. The funding lens cannot operate without a scoreable liability series. Neither result says that pressure was absent. It says the supplied replay cannot establish that either lens observed it first.

That distinction becomes sharper under the historical construction label: `PERIOD_END_PROXY_CONSTRUCTION_PIT`. The record is not validated-backtest eligible, not real-money eligible, and has no bitemporal input contract. Where an explicit publication clock is absent, availability is proxied by period end plus 60 days. The dossier also states that lead times are optimistic. A period-end proxy may impose a conservative delay convention, but it still does not prove the actual information set available to a lender, depositor, investor, or supervisor at that time.

The broader replay gives context but cannot fill this institution’s gaps. Across failed institutions, the PCA summary reports 15 cases, with 5 entering the action zone first and a median lead of 41 months. The funding summary also reports 15 failed institutions, but only 10 have liability disclosures; the funding signal fired first in 4, with a median lead of 38 months. Those are cohort descriptions, not proof that Rupee Co-operative Bank travelled either path. The [validation record](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/validation) preserves those limits.

## Why the warning mattered

The warning here was epistemic. A desk seeking to rank balance-sheet stress needed evidence on supervisory-threshold inputs or liabilities, with a credible availability date. The replay does not provide a scoreable funding series and does not provide a first PCA action-zone observation. The proper result is an unresolved institution-specific record.

That matters because absence is easily misread. “No signal” can mean that a threshold did not fire on available inputs. “No score” can mean that the needed inputs were unavailable or unusable. “No market-price signal” would mean something else again: that a market-based measure was absent, unavailable, or did not cross its own rule. These states cannot honestly be collapsed into “no risk.”

The methodology says components are replayed independently on a 48-institution construction-PIT record and fused only for presentation. It also says the conformal alarm is diagnostic, with no score or tier authority pending prospective revalidation. Those constraints are not footnotes. They prevent a model derivation from being presented as a contemporaneous observation.

## The strongest counter-case

The strongest counter-case can defeat any stronger thesis: this replay may be too incomplete to say which balance sheet would have felt stress first, or whether either disclosed lens would have given a useful warning before the event. Pressure may have emerged outside the captured series, moved more quickly than the filing proxy, or remained outside the supplied public record.

The validation statistics reinforce caution. The hazard panel contains 205 rows, 9 events, and 27 institutions, while 179 censored or unusable rows were excluded. Leave-one-institution-out row AUC is 0.752, with a CI95 range of 0.338 to 1.0. The temporal diagnostic AUC is 0.645, below the 0.65 gate, and failed that gate. On the same held-out rows, the heuristic AUC is 0.799.

Those figures do not establish that the screen is useless. They do establish that historical discrimination is uncertain and that construction-PIT diagnostics cannot be promoted into a tradable or decision-ready backtest. The counter-case therefore defeats any assertion that Rupee Co-operative Bank was cleanly flagged. It does not defeat the narrower thesis that the honest output is a documented blind spot rather than reassurance.

## What today's board shares

Today’s board is a separate comparison, not historical evidence about this institution. As of 2026-09-01, it reports 0 red, 1 orange, 3 yellow, and 15 green institutions. Utkarsh Small Finance Bank is orange, with a score of 74.9 and a dossier as of 2025-03-31 that is 18 months old. Belstar Microfinance Limited is yellow at 77.8, as of 2026-03-31 and 6 months old. ESAF Small Finance Bank is yellow at 66.0, as of 2025-09-30 and 12 months old, with market distance-to-default of 1.927 and the `market_dd_below_2` signal.

These are current screen states, not forecasts. The board excludes 21 stale institutions, and nothing older than 24 months is presented as current. Its market layer uses daily auto-adjusted Yahoo Finance closes through 2026-08-11, documented in the [market evidence index](https://api.liquilens.in/api/evidence/markets). An absent institution is not thereby green; Rupee Co-operative Bank’s replay shows why.

## The next falsifiable test

This account can be disproved with a genuinely bitemporal, pre-event public record. It would need dated filings or disclosures, a verified publication clock, and scoreable PCA or liability-series inputs. If that record showed a timely action-zone breach or funding signal, the replay should identify the first lens and its lead time.

If it instead showed neither signal before the event despite verified timely availability, the claim that the key warning was an evidence boundary would be weakened. Either result would be more informative than retrospective reconstruction from later dates. Until then, the missing data must remain visible rather than being converted into a signal.

## Follow the pressure chain

For a risk committee, the sequence is procedural: establish the filing or publication date; test whether supervisory-threshold inputs are scoreable; test whether liability disclosures exist; then separate any market repricing observation from the filing-based evidence. A missing link stops the inference chain. It does not complete it.

LiquiLens addresses **institution and lender balance-sheet risk**. Seiche addresses **system dollar-funding capacity**, as described in the [Seiche overview](https://api.seiche.info/api/overview). Undertow addresses **market liquidity and executable exit capacity**, as shown on the [Undertow board](https://api.seiche.info/undertow/board.json). The questions can be related, but system funding, an institution balance sheet, and executable market exit are not interchangeable measurements.

## Sources, method, and limits

The core materials are the [Rupee Co-operative Bank replay](https://liquilens.in/replay/rupee-co-operative-bank/), the [Failure Radar board](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/board), the [historical validation file](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/validation), and the [market evidence index](https://api.liquilens.in/api/evidence/markets). Additional desk material is available through [LiquiLens research](https://liquilens.in/research/) and the [investigations archive](https://liquilens.in/investigations/).

This is a public-disclosure replay with period-end proxy construction timing, not a validated backtest or a real-money test. Lead times are optimistic. Fraud-masked filings can appear compliant to threshold engines; this case is not fraud-masked, but that general limitation remains. **This is not investment advice.**
